collection.title: 3D Molecule Viewer & Mechanisms
collection.description: Interactive 3D molecules and organic reaction mechanisms for Class 11-12 Chemistry

steps.label: Propene (Reactant)
steps.annotation: H–Br approaches the C=C π bond
steps.explanation: Markovnikov's Rule: H⁺ from HBr adds to the carbon with more hydrogens (C1). The π electrons attract the electrophile.

steps.label: 2° Carbocation Intermediate
steps.explanation: H⁺ adds to C1, forming a more stable secondary carbocation at C2. Stability order: 3° > 2° > 1°.

steps.label: 2-Bromopropane (Product)
steps.annotation: Br⁻ attacks the carbocation at C2
steps.explanation: Bromide ion attacks the electrophilic C2, giving the Markovnikov product 2-bromopropane. Anti-Markovnikov addition would give 1-bromopropane.

steps.label: Bromomethane (Reactant)
steps.annotation: Nucleophile OH⁻ approaches back of C–Br bond (180°)
steps.explanation: SN2 is concerted — bond formation and breaking happen simultaneously. Favoured by primary substrates and strong nucleophiles in polar aprotic solvents.

steps.label: Transition State
steps.explanation: At the transition state, carbon is simultaneously bonded to both OH and Br. Configuration inverts — Walden Inversion.

steps.label: Methanol + Br⁻ (Product)
steps.explanation: Product methanol forms with complete inversion of configuration. SN2 shows second-order kinetics: rate = k[substrate][nucleophile].

steps.label: Acetic Acid + H⁺ Catalyst
steps.explanation: H⁺ (acid catalyst) protonates the C=O oxygen, making the carbonyl carbon highly electrophilic. Reaction is reversible — Le Chatelier's principle applies.

steps.label: Nucleophilic Addition of Ethanol
steps.annotation: O of ethanol attacks activated carbonyl C
steps.explanation: Ethanol oxygen attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a tetrahedral intermediate. A proton transfer follows.

steps.label: Ethyl Acetate + H₂O (Product)
steps.explanation: Loss of water (dehydration) gives ethyl acetate. Removing water or using excess alcohol drives the equilibrium toward product (Fischer esterification).

steps.label: Acetaldehyde + NaOH
steps.annotation: Base removes α-hydrogen to form enolate
steps.explanation: NaOH removes an α-hydrogen from acetaldehyde, forming a resonance-stabilised enolate ion. The α-carbon becomes nucleophilic.

steps.label: Enolate Attacks Second Carbonyl
steps.explanation: The enolate attacks the carbonyl of a second acetaldehyde molecule, forming a β-hydroxy aldehyde (the 'aldol' — aldehyde + alcohol).

steps.label: Crotonaldehyde (Condensation Product)
steps.annotation: Dehydration gives α,β-unsaturated aldehyde on heating
steps.explanation: On heating, the aldol loses water to give crotonaldehyde (but-2-enal). Aldol condensation is key in biosynthesis of complex carbon skeletons.
